source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: Next, consider non-finite predicative agreement. In (14) and (15), (a) represents the finite version of predication, (b) shows the same predication structure embedded as a subject complement clause. The pair in (14) built on an adjective shows that an adjective is invariably interpreted as a predicate in both finite and embedded structures. The pair in (15) shows that a noun is interpreted as predicative with a purely predicative morpheme but as a possessee licensing a possessor if the morpheme is ambiguous between predicative and possessive.
